name: John Cockerill India Ltd
tagline: Steel-processing equipment maker (ex-CMI FPE) with an order book inflecting hard on CRGO/CRNO electrical-steel localisation and a Belgium metals-business consolidation -- but wafer-thin margins, a currently loss-making quarter and a ~110x P/E make the multibagger case unconfirmed
business_overview: John Cockerill India (formerly CMI FPE) designs, manufactures and commissions equipment for the steel industry -- cold rolling mills, skin-pass mills, processing and coating lines, and newer Jet Vapor Deposition (JVD) coating technology. It is the listed Indian arm of Belgium's John Cockerill group. Key near-term driver is supplying processing lines for domestic grain-oriented / cold-rolled non-grain-oriented (CRGO/CRNO) electrical steel -- the material that goes into transformer and motor cores, currently largely imported into India. NOTE: the group's green-hydrogen/electrolyser and defence businesses sit in the Belgian parent, NOT the listed Indian entity (management-confirmed repeatedly).
fundamentals_table: Standalone revenue ~Rs 150 Cr (+83% YoY) but a net LOSS of ~Rs 4.6 Cr; consolidated revenue ~Rs 345 Cr (+56% YoY), EBITDA ~Rs 4.9 Cr (1.4% margin)

Consolidated ~Rs 4,500 Cr / standalone ~Rs 2,200 Cr; Q2 order intake ~Rs 1,200 Cr; execution up to 3 years. JCIL's share of the JSW Vijayanagar CRNO order is ~Rs 550 Cr (of the Rs 1,250-1,300 Cr headline)
Almost debt-free; promoter (John Cockerill) reduced 75% -> 70.4%, expected back above 72% via convertible preference shares; nil pledge
fundamentals_narrative: The trailing record is poor -- flat sales for five years, single-digit ROE, and the most recent quarter swung to a small net loss on a 1.4% consolidated EBITDA margin despite an 83% standalone revenue jump. What has changed is forward-looking: order book +74% YoY with unusually large tickets (Rs 200-1,300 Cr), a Rs 1,250-1,300 Cr JSW CRNO line, and a pending acquisition of John Cockerill Metals International (Belgium) for EUR 50m deferred zero-interest over 5 years that management frames as adding ~Rs 1,000 Cr of revenue capability. So the pattern is weak average + strong specific recent order inflection + credible catalyst, in a small-cap -- but margins are unproven and the multiple already discounts a lot.
technical_read: Not independently charted this pass. Stock has re-rated sharply (P/E ~110x) on the order-book story; a fundamentals-led 'unconfirmed 10x' verdict does not hinge on the chart.
sentiment_summary: Small but engaged thread (25 posts) started by SEBI RA Ayush Agrawal (@imicrocap) as a decarbonisation case study. Recent posts (Dec-2025 to Aug-2026) are constructive: Md_Uzair and Satishwe detailing the Belgium consolidation, JVD first commercial orders expected 2026, Volteron electrolysis-ironmaking licence, and marquee investors Ramesh Damani (~Rs 13 Cr) and Chetan Shah (~Rs 12 Cr) taking stakes in Dec-2025. Manav (Jan-2026) and others repeatedly clarify that the sexier hydrogen and defence lines are in the Belgian parent, not the listco. Arka (Aug-2026) highlights the sheer size of order tickets relative to market cap.
community_signal: Satishwe (trusted, elevated-tier) posted a detailed, constructive consolidation-and-technology update on 2025-12-31 (post #21, 7 loves) -- bullish framing of the Belgium acquisition economics and new tech, though not an explicit dated buy call at a stated price. Nitya_Shah (non-trusted, another RA) disclosed a BUY recommendation back in 2023. Overall community tone: high interest, aware that margins and the listed-entity scope are the open questions.

bse_notes: No governance red flag: promoter ~70.4% with nil pledge, almost debt-free. Older thread posts flagged high contingent liabilities vs net worth -- a recurring feature of the project-equipment model (bank guarantees / advance guarantees), worth monitoring but not a formal red flag. Disclosure quality around group-entity boundaries (which businesses sit in the listco) has been questioned by forum members.
bull_case: Order book +74% YoY with very large tickets relative to a ~Rs 3,050 Cr market cap -- Rs 1,250-1,300 Cr JSW CRNO line alone is ~4x annual revenue
CRGO/CRNO electrical-steel processing-line demand is a genuine India import-substitution wave feeding the transformer/grid supply chain (JSW, others building domestic electrical-steel capacity)
Belgium John Cockerill Metals International consolidation could roughly double revenue capability for EUR 50m deferred zero-interest -- accretive if margins hold
Marquee investors (Ramesh Damani, Chetan Shah) entered Dec-2025; JVD coating tech commercialising; 3-year steel import tariffs support domestic steel capex
Debt-free, ~70% promoter holding, MNC parent with technology backward-integration
bear_case: Wafer-thin, volatile margins are a structural feature of the equipment business -- Q1 FY27 was a net loss at 1.4% consolidated EBITDA margin despite +56-83% revenue growth
P/E ~110x already prices in a large execution-and-margin improvement that has not shown up in reported numbers
The green-hydrogen/electrolyser and defence optionality that drives the 'decarbonisation' narrative is in the Belgian parent, NOT the listed entity
Five years of flat sales and single-digit ROE; historically a cyclical, low-return project-equipment maker losing share vs industry growth
Belgium acquisition adds integration risk and consolidates lower-margin global subsidiaries; valuation gap between EUR 50m price and 'Rs 1,000 Cr revenue' claim unexplained on the thread
verdict_headline: Order-book inflection and Belgium consolidation give a real multibagger path, but margins and listed-entity scope keep it strictly unconfirmed
verdict_reasoning: Theme match: priority-1 'Grid / transmission equipment (transformers, HV switchgear, HVDC, CRGO, insulators)' -- the CRGO/CRNO electrical-steel processing lines JCIL supplies are direct import-substitution inputs to the transformer/grid chain.

Trailing-average-vs-live-inflection rule applied: weak 5-yr average, but a strong specific recent inflection (order book +74% YoY, Rs 1,300 Cr JSW CRNO line, Belgium consolidation, marquee investors) in a Rs 3,050 Cr small-cap -> label 10x-in-2-3-years at LOW conviction with an explicit unconfirmed caveat, not 'neither'.

UNCONFIRMED: Q1 FY27 is loss-making at 1.4% EBITDA margin; P/E ~110x already discounts a big improvement; hydrogen/defence optionality is in the Belgian parent, not the listco. Margin proof-out over the next 2-3 quarters is the swing factor.
No red flag (promoter ~70%, nil pledge, debt-free). Conviction Low; no 30-day revisit (conviction below Medium-High).

deep_dive.conviction_update: Low -> Low. Q2 CY26 confirmed the order-book inflection is real and bigger than recorded (consolidated book ~Rs 4,500 Cr) but also confirmed the margin problem is unresolved - a second straight quarter of 80%+ revenue growth with no profit. At ~110x P/E the market already prices the improvement; unchanged at Low pending an actual margin print.

value_chain.theme: Grid / transmission equipment (transformers, HV switchgear, HVDC, CRGO, insulators)
value_chain.position: Capital-equipment supplier to steelmakers -- cold rolling / skin-pass / processing and coating lines, and specifically CRGO/CRNO electrical-steel processing lines whose output feeds transformer and motor cores
value_chain.bottleneck_node: Domestic electrical-steel (CRGO/CRNO) processing capacity -- India imports most of its grain-oriented electrical steel; equipment to localise it is the choke point JCIL sells into
value_chain.note: Very few players build these lines; JCIL's edge is the John Cockerill parent's technology and an installed-base relationship with Indian steelmakers. Demand driver is the India CRGO import-substitution push (JSW electrical-steel capex, transformer-industry pull). Order pipeline visibility is strong; the open question is JCIL's own execution margin, not end-demand.

earnings_quality.normalised_note: The risk is the reverse of a peak - reported EBITDA margin is ~1-1.4%, far BELOW any defensible through-cycle level for the equipment business (historically mid-single-digit). Management asserts a recovery to H2 CY26; unproven.

growth_trajectory.last_quarters_note: Standalone revenue YoY: +83% (Q1 to Jun-2026), +82% (Q2 CY26); consolidated +56% then +18%. Order intake lumpy - a single Rs 1,200-1,300 Cr JSW ticket dominates. PAT swung from +Rs 1.7 Cr to -Rs 4.6 Cr YoY.
growth_trajectory.reverse_pe_note: Order/project business - treat as lumpy/neutral for haircut purposes. ~110x needs a margin step-change the reported numbers have not begun to show; rate-of-change on profit is negative.

management_quality.capital_allocation: Historically low-return (3-yr ROE ~6%); now deploying into a Belgium acquisition (EUR 50m deferred) and JVD/Volteron technology licences. Almost debt-free. The EUR 50m-for-Rs 1,000 Cr-revenue framing is unexplained on the thread.
management_quality.capability_ladder_note: Explicit move up the value curve: JVD coating tech, Volteron electrolysis ironmaking licence, and consolidating the parent's metals business into the listco

track_record.note: FY22-FY25 verifiable: no single year cleared both revenue growth >=10% and ROCE >=15% - five-year sales CAGR ~0.9%, 3-yr ROE ~6%. This is an established under-performer, not a young company, so a zero count is a genuine signal. The entire bull case rests on a forward inflection, not the record.

open_questions: fcf_conversion not derivable cleanly this pass - project-equipment cash flows swing with advances/milestones; the recent quarters' losses make trailing conversion unreliable rather than simply negative

four_box.note: value_chain: CRGO/CRNO import-substitution is a real choke point, 'very few players build these lines' (moat=yes); consolidated order book ~Rs 4,500 Cr, ~1.5x mcap (tam=yes); tailwind=yes (India electrical-steel localisation + grid capex); P/E ~110x on ~1% EBITDA margin already discounts a big improvement (valuation=no).
